Calculate the displacement vector from the center: $\Delta u = u - x_0$, $\Delta v = v - y_0$ [S1].

The claim states that the displacement vector from the center is calculated as $Δu = u - x_0$ and $Δv = v - y_0$. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines the rotated coordinates $x_θ$ and $y_θ$ using the terms $(u - x_0)$ and $(v - y_0)$. Specifically, the equations provided are $x_θ = cos θ (u - x_0) - sin θ (v - y_0) + x_0$ and $y_θ = sin θ (u - x_0) + cos θ (v - y_0) + y_0$. In the context of 2D rotation matrices, $(u - x_0)$ and $(v - y_0)$ represent the displacement components of the point $(u, v)$ relative to the center $(x_0, y_0)$ before rotation. Therefore, the evidence supports the definition of these terms as the displacement components.
